subject: Run 5 finished: the corrected build stood itself down for no edge
body:
Tenth version. Run 5 finished, and it is the one that mattered.

    CALIBRATION RESULT  |  STAND DOWN  |  cause: NO-EDGE
    ghost 20.0% WR   E[R] -0.70R   PF 0.15   2 of 6 gates   walk-forward fragile
    100 minutes, 5 of 6 phases fully verified, zero live trades armed

This is the first calibration on a build where all four of this week's defects were fixed at once
-- the score scale, the 68 wrong-timeframe reads, the threshold desync, and the silenced evidence
lines. Runs 1 through 4 each still carried at least one. So this is the first time the system's own
gates have judged an instrument that was measuring what it thought it was measuring.

It said no edge, and refused to trade.

I want to be careful about how that reads, because there are two ways to take it and only one is
right. A calibration that stands itself down is a WORKING calibration. The failure mode would have
been arming on 20% win rate at a profit factor of 0.15. It declined, unprompted, which is exactly
what your own C8.3 criterion asks the system to do as evidence weakens. The risk machinery works.
It is the signal that is not there.

And it now agrees with everything else. Four independent routes, one answer:

    the per-class C4 record        inconclusive, nothing clears the bar
    every component's IC curve     nothing clears at 899 registered tests
    the measurement-wall maths     the viable horizons are below the detection floor
    the ghost rescue sweep         zero trades at every threshold of 55 or above

C6.3 and C6.4 are still not met even with a fourth calibration in hand, and the reason is worth
knowing: Type I and Type II rates are measurable in ZERO of the four runs. The EA does not record
them per calibration. So that half is blocked on instrumentation, not on performance -- it cannot
improve until the EA writes the numbers down. Forecast error is not falling either (3.83 -> 9.57).

BOARD: 30 of 46 automated now, 13 MET. C2.2 earned tonight -- zero block sequence gaps in a full
run, which needed a full run to prove. C5.1 earned too (confidence-adjusted Kelly, and it really
does ramp from zero at zero trades to full weight at 300).

TWO THINGS WAITING ON YOU:

1. The risk floors from earlier (0.5% hardcoded vs your 1.5% MinRiskPercent). Still open.

2. C5.2 says "drawdown fade at k=2". Your fade is 1 - dd/0.22, which is linear with a coefficient
of 4.55. As an exponent it is 1. Neither reading gives 2 -- though setting KellyDDBudget to 50
would give exactly k=2. I have left the criterion undecided rather than guess what k means. What
did you intend?

AND ONE MORE THING I FOUND. You have two drawdown mechanisms. The Kelly fade uses a true
high-water mark. The other one -- the continuous lot taper -- computes its peak as
max(current equity, starting balance). Above your starting balance that just equals current equity,
so its drawdown is always zero and the taper can never fire. An account that doubled and gave back
a quarter is 25% down from its peak and this one sees 0%. It only ever engages below the starting
balance. The real high-water mark is in the same struct, two lines of code away.

Terminal is still open, so nothing has shipped. There are now five EA edits queued for the moment
you close it.
